name: Produce Waste Specialist
failure_modes: inflated weight estimates for small volumes
checks: visible rot or damage consistent with waste
notes: Produce waste is the most common submission. 38 lbs/week family baseline. Leafy greens weigh less than claimed more often than not.

name: Bakery Waste Specialist
failure_modes: end-of-day photos not representing actual waste
notes: Bakery waste is predictable — end of day, daily. Photos at opening time are suspicious.

name: Dairy Waste Specialist
failure_modes: photos of product still on shelf
notes: Dairy waste often involves liquid weight. 1 gallon milk = 8.6 lbs. Count containers.

name: Meat and Protein Waste Specialist
failure_modes: claimed weights significantly exceed visible volume
notes: Meat waste is high value and high weight. 1 lb of meat is roughly the size of a fist. Scale claims carefully.

name: Prepared Food Waste Specialist
failure_modes: single meal counts inflated to bulk weight
checks: time of submission consistent with service hours
notes: Prepared food waste from restaurants and institutions. Container weight can be 30-40% of total.

name: Corporate Waste Specialist
failure_modes: single store vs distribution center confusion
sustainability report numbers vs actual waste
checks: not labeled as donated or redistributed
notes: Corporate waste reports are highest value. Distribution centers can generate thousands of lbs daily. Verify source type.

name: Grocery Retail Waste Specialist
failure_modes: photos from dumpster not loading dock
checks: no non-food items in claimed weight
notes: Grocery waste is consistent and predictable. Produce, bakery, deli, dairy in that order by volume.

name: School and Institutional Food Waste Specialist
failure_modes: cafeteria tray waste vs bulk waste confusion
checks: source identified as school or institution
notes: School food waste is significant and systematic. USDA school lunch waste is documented and chronic.
